mechanism_narrative: The sustained four-week decline in WORKPLACES mobility (-5.6 to -20.6) reflects reduced commuting and associated incidental shopping trips, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as the same structural reduction in office-linked foot traffic persists.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline or remaining flat, indicating decoupling of commuting and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls below -22 percent for two consecutive weeks, it signals an active mobility-restriction policy phase that will mechanically reduce access to retail and recreation sites, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -22 points for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -18.1 to -24.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing below -22 for two consecutive weeks, despite continued transit suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and rise in RESIDENTIAL indicate a combined shift toward home-centered living that compounds to suppress discretionary retail visits more strongly than either series would alone, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines and RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -5.6 to -20.6 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 11.1 to 16.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline further even though both WORKPLACES keeps falling and RESIDENTIAL keeps rising together for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The rise in GROCERY_PHARM (6.0 to 10.6) under a tightening-restrictions regime reflects anticipatory stockpiling ahead of expected mobility curbs; this substitution behavior will further depress RETAIL_REC as households front-load essential purchases and avoid non-essential retail trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC declines in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose each week from 6.0 to 10.6 while RETAIL_REC fell from -13.4 to -15.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within one week even as GROCERY_PHARM continues to climb, showing no substitution linkage.

mechanism_narrative: The steady improvement in PARKS (-20.1 to -14.7) reflects a seasonal or weather-driven shift of discretionary outdoor activity away from indoor retail and recreation venues, which will keep RETAIL_REC subdued over the next week as outdoor substitution continues.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved each week from -20.1 to -14.7 while RETAIL_REC declined
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with continued PARKS improvement, indicating no substitution effect between outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES exceeding 10 points, as occurred from t-1w to t-0w (-10.6 to -20.6), signals an abrupt activity shock that will propagate into reduced commuter-adjacent retail visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 10 points from -10.6 to -20.6 in the final week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline further within two weeks of a WORKPLACES week-on-week drop exceeding 10 points.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both worsened every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or improves over four weeks despite continued joint decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, indicating no compounding effect.

candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises for three or more consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose every week from 11.1 to 16.4 over four weeks
